correctness.rationale: Variance ODE yields explicit centered Gaussians; their symmetrized directed KL equals the specified rational variance reward. Direct differentiation proves a single convex-to-concave inflection of the reward, hence a unique positive root of xF'(x)-F(x); the tangent line and original concave tail give the exact least concave majorant. Jensen and contact-point equality prove the optimum and unique deterministic / unattainable two-point burst regimes for every finite-mean renewal law. A simple-root Taylor expansion supplies the sharp square-root small-reset-variance law. Python standard-library verification independently passed 7,123 finite assertions; universal statements rely on proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The evaluated new statement optimizes the endpoint Gaussian Jeffreys reward over every positive renewal waiting-time law with fixed mean and proves the unique tangent, deterministic/burst regime classification, and cold-width square-root transition. Farago derives endpoint KL for harmonic Gaussian resetting but treats prescribed Poisson and periodic protocols, not a fixed-mean arbitrary-law envelope. Olsen et al. treat physical trap resetting work and its control variables; Mori et al. treat Poisson reset positions and path-level entropy production. The classical renewal-reward theorem and concavification are acknowledged as prior general tools, not claimed novel. The distinct possible implication from a broader prior concave-envelope theorem remains a specific risk and priority is not certified.

value.rationale: For an OU model of the finite-width resetting engine, the physically motivated question is to optimize the full iid waiting-time law under a mean-cycle-time resource. The theorem gives an explicit single boundary separating regular from burst-like timing, sharp equality and nonattainment classification, and a singular square-root dependence on the reset variance. This improves on restricting attention to Poissonian or deterministic clocks and provides a direct protocol-design benchmark, without conflating it with full entropy production.
